newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WENGER AT ODDS WITH DUTCH OVER BERGKAMP CALL-UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WENGER AT ODDS WITH DUTCH OVER BERGKAMP CALL-UP.

text.p: Arsenal's new manager Arsene Wenger is on a collision course with the Dutch national side over striker Dennis Bergkamp's latest injury.

Dutch coach Guus Hiddink has named Bergkamp in his squad for Saturday's World Cup qualifying match against Wales even though the striker has a hamstring strain which has kept him out of the Arsenal side since mid-September.
Asked if he thought Hiddink would deploy Bergkamp against the Welsh, Wenger said: "I hope he does not as Dennis has not been able to train for nearly three weeks.
"I don't see how they could make him play. It is dangerous and far too soon after he suffered the injury."
Wenger's assistant Pat Rice said the 27-year-old forward was still doubtful for Arsenal's league clash against Blackburn on October 12.
"Dennis certainly had no chance for last Saturday's match against Sunderland and we have been determined not to rush him back too early for fear of quickly losing him again," Rice said.
"But Holland told us they wanted to assess his fitness for themselves and we could not really refuse."

Under FIFA rules, national sides have a six-day priority over club sides in naming players for World Cup qualifiers. Bergkamp came close to missing the start of the English league season after damaging a knee playing for the Netherlands in the European championship in June.
In December last year he played for the Dutch against the Republic of Ireland despite a calf injury, and subsequently missed three Arsenal fixtures.
